en: Some species of bamboo are the fastest-growing plants in the world, capable of growing up to 91 centimeters in a single day.
A blue whale's tongue alone weighs approximately 2,700 kilograms, which is about the same weight as a fully grown African elephant.
The Arctic tern flies an average of 70,000 kilometers each year during its migration, the longest distance traveled by any animal in the world.
A human baby is born with around 300 bones, but many fuse together as they grow, leaving an adult with exactly 206 bones.
The average human heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping roughly 7,500 liters of blood throughout the entire body.
A thirsty camel can drink up to 200 liters of water in just 13 minutes to survive in hot, dry desert ecosystems.
Adult mayflies have the shortest lifespan of any insect, living for only 24 hours or less just long enough to mate and lay eggs.
The Etruscan shrew has the fastest metabolism of any mammal, with its tiny heart beating up to 1,500 times per minute.
A single orchid seed pod can contain up to four million tiny seeds, which is far more than most other plants produce.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird of the Philippines, has a massive wingspan measuring up to two meters from wing tip to wing tip.
If you uncoiled all the DNA in a single human cell and stretched it out, it would measure about two meters long.
A single leafcutter ant colony can contain up to eight million individual worker ants living in underground nests spanning 30 square meters.
